h1: Prediabetes medication: what the prevention trials showed
dek: No medicine is approved in the US specifically for prediabetes. Metformin has the longest record, cutting diabetes onset by 31% in the Diabetes Prevention Program, less than lifestyle change did; semaglutide and tirzepatide showed larger effects in people with obesity.
scope: Informational intent only. Price, coverage and where-to-get queries are out of scope and not mapped.

information_gain: The only page on this SERP to put every randomised prevention trial (DPP, DPPOS, STOP-NIDDM, ACT NOW, STEP, SELECT, SURMOUNT-1) in one table with its population and trade-off, to report that the metformin effect fell from 31% to 18% over 15 years, and to state that the GLP-1 effects were measured on treatment, with diabetes rates rising after tirzepatide stopped.
serp_format_rewarded: Featured snippet and AI Overview with People Also Ask: a direct first-paragraph answer (no FDA-approved drug; metformin 31% vs lifestyle 58%), then a comparison table and short question-led sections.
